dedupe_keys.name: epa disaster debris recovery tool ddrt recyclers and landfills for disaster debris

description: The Disaster Debris Recovery Tool is an interactive map and dataset of facilities that can take the materials left after a disaster, so that planners and responders can route debris to recycling and safe disposal, not open dumping. The US Environmental Protection Agency created it in its Region 5 office in 2010 and has since extended it nationwide. It lists more than 20,000 facilities in twelve categories, including construction and demolition recyclers, concrete and asphalt, metals, electronics, household hazardous waste, vegetative waste, vehicles and tyres, and municipal solid waste and construction landfills, across all 50 states, Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands and, since the August 2026 update, the Pacific Islands. Each facility record now carries its data source and last update date. The web map, a national GIS feature service and downloadable data are free as a US government product. Caveats: facility capacity and acceptance rules are not guaranteed and should be confirmed with operators before an event, and the list mixes sources of different ages. Simulation uses: planning debris removal and routing after floods, hurricanes and wildfires, estimating recovery time when landfills or recyclers are damaged, and building the waste side of post-disaster recovery models. Related records: the Congressional Research Service report on disaster debris management (data-crs-disaster-debris-management-r44941) explains the federal roles, and the EPA Recycling Infrastructure and Market Opportunities Map (data-epa-recycling-infrastructure-market-opportunities-map) covers routine recycling plants.
